panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: CT angiographic reconstruction from Case 1 demonstrates extensive branch-artery occlusions characteristic of Takayasu arteritis, with additional documented right vertebral artery stenosis. B: Second CT angiographic reconstruction from the same case shows extensive large- and medium-vessel occlusions characteristic of Takayasu arteritis, with additional documented right vertebral artery stenosis.

panels.figure_caption: (A, B) Case 1: computed tomography (CT) angiography demonstrating occlusion of the brachiocephalic artery, the right common and internal carotid arteries, the ipsilateral subclavian and axillary arteries, and the V1 segment of the right vertebral artery. 1: occlusion of the brachiocephalic artery; 2: complete occlusion of the right common carotid artery; 3: right subclavian; 4: stenosis of the V1 segment of the right vertebral artery; 5: right vertebral artery; 6: left common carotid artery; 7: left internal carotid artery; 8: left external carotid artery; 9: left vertebral artery
in_text_mentions: ntext of systemic inflammation. Brain imaging confirmed an ischemic stroke in the right middle cerebral artery territory. CT angiography and MR angiography demonstrated multiple arterial lesions involving the carotid arteries (Figures 1, 2). Doppler ultrasound of the supra-aortic vessels showed circumferential hypoechoic wall thickening of the carotid arteries (“macaroni sign”), consistent with inflammatory involvement (Figure 3). High-dose corticosteroid therapy (1 mg/kg/day) was initiated, along with antiplatelet therapy. The clinical course was favorable, with partial neurological recovery.

in_text_mentions: moglobin at 7 g/dL (reference range 12-16 g/dL); serum ferritin was 367 µg/L. Doppler ultrasound of the supra-aortic vessels demonstrated circumferential hypoechoic wall thickening of the carotid arteries (“macaroni sign”), indicative of active inflammatory involvement (Figure 4). Vascular imaging using CT angiography and MR angiography revealed extensive and predominant involvement of the carotid arteries, with complete occlusion of the right internal carotid artery. As illustrated in Figure 5, imaging demonstrated severe carotid involvement, consistent with advanced-stage Takayasu arteritis.
